title: Singapore's Economic Outlook Given Rising Inflation and Government's Plans to Assist Businesses and Singaporeans
what_it_is: Singapore's Economic Outlook Given Rising Inflation and Government's Plans to Assist Businesses and Singaporeans

sections.label: MAS inflation forecasts
sections.summary: MAS Core Inflation rose to 3.6% year-on-year in May, and CPI-All Items inflation rose to 5.6%, with full-year averages projected at 2.5% to 3.5% and 4.5% to 5.5%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: MAS Core Inflation picked up to 3.6% year-on-year in May, from 3.3% in April and 2.5% in the first quarter of the year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: CPI-All Items inflation, which includes private transport and accommodation costs, rose to 5.6% year-on-year in May, from 5.4% in April and 4.6% in the first quarter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: For the year as a whole, MAS Core Inflation is expected to average 2.5% to 3.5%, while CPI-All Items inflation is projected to average 4.5% to 5.5%.

sections.label: MTI 2022 GDP forecast
sections.summary: MTI expects the Singapore economy to expand by 3% to 5% in 2022, with growth likely in the lower half of the range.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Overall, MTI expects the Singapore economy to expand by 3% to 5% in 2022, with growth likely to come in at the lower half of the forecast range.

sections.label: GDP growth forecast on track
sections.summary: MTI assesses GDP growth is on track to come within the 3% to 5% forecast range, which represents above-trend growth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: To the specific points that the Member raised, if you take into account this expected recovery and the resilient performance of some of the outward-oriented sectors, such as our electronics cluster, MTI's assessment is that GDP growth is on track to come in within the official forecast range mentioned earlier of between 3% and 5%, notwithstanding external shocks or growing headwinds in the economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: This growth forecast actually represents above-trend growth because in the five years prior to the pandemic, GDP growth averaged about 3.2% per annum.

sections.label: Tight labour market outlook
sections.summary: Labour market conditions are expected to remain tight but significant overheating is unlikely, with non-resident worker inflows helping alleviate manpower shortages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: We all know that labour market conditions are tight.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: We expect them to remain tight but a significant overheating of the labour market is unlikely.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Following the significant easing of border measures since end-March, the in-flow of non-resident workers should help to alleviate manpower shortages and also moderate labour cost pressures in the coming months.

sections.label: Consumer response to higher prices
sections.summary: Higher prices will lead to some consumer adjustments, but recent inflation has not led to significant cut-backs in household consumption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Higher prices will lead to some adjustments in consumer behaviour, as consumers substitute between products, as well as services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Thus far, the higher inflation readings in recent months have not led to any significant cut-backs, at least in household consumption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: The latest private consumption, retail sales and F&B sales indices point to firm consumption spending.

sections.label: Dian Xiao Er revenue expectation
sections.summary: Dian Xiao Er expects its revenue to increase by 40% from FY2021 to FY2023, based on recent performances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Dian Xiao Er is expecting its revenue to increase by 40% from FY2021 to FY2023, based on this recent performances.
